alignments.note: Waw rendered by the connective Then (rule 14).

מִן of מֵעָלַי: the ASV promotes the preposition's object to the direct object 'me' and states nothing for the preposition's own relation (rule 40). Competing reading: מֵעַל → 'of' as a compound after the recasting 'stripped me of'; but that 'of' reaches the verb's own bare object כְּבוֹדִי and is placed by rule 44.
עַל of מֵעָלַי silenced by the same recasting (rule 40); each morpheme of the unrendered compound is its own unit (rule 2).
Suffix on the silenced preposition takes the object pronoun 'me' (rule 40).

'He hath stripped ... of': כְּבוֹדִי is a bare direct object in the Hebrew and the English verb reaches it only through the supplied 'of', which joins the verb's unit under rule 44's supplied-preposition clause, discontinuous around 'me' (rule 25).
Supplied 'the' on the construct (rule 29).
Construct relation recast with 'from', which belongs to the rectum (rule 19).

review_notes: Corrected the placement of 'of': the Hebrew writes glory as the bare direct object and 'from upon me' as the ablative; the ASV's 'stripped me of my glory' inverts the two, so 'of' is the verb's supplied preposition to its own object (rule 44) and מֵעַל is left with no word for its relation (rule 40). Compare JOB.19.13, where the same מֵעָלַי is rendered directly as 'from me' and keeps the word.

review_notes: Variant unit v001 covers s014–s015; the projection's r00-base reading (שַׁ + דּוּן) is among those the English permits, so no FALLBACK EXCLUDED handling applies.

variant_decisions.evidence: ASV 'That ye may know there is a judgment' renders relative ש + דין 'judgment' either way; the qere/ketiv difference is a vowel-letter spelling of the same word and no English wording or italicized supply distinguishes it. The only note ('Or, wrathful are') is alternative_rendering on 'wrath bringeth' and does not touch this unit. Retain the qere base fallback.
